subject: zoology_2
question_text: Write an essay on common genetic disorders.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book pp.24-25, LAQ 9. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: The two categories
steps.why: One kind is caused by a change in a single gene and the other by a change in a whole chromosome, so the two are counted separately.
steps.memory_tip: Mendelian = one gene. Chromosomal = a whole chromosome.
steps.margin_note: Name both categories, then take them in order.
lines: Genetic disorders are associated with genes
or chromosomes. They fall into two
categories:
1. Mendelian disorders
2. Chromosomal disorders
These show Mendelian inheritance. They are
caused by a single mutation in DNA, so they
are called monogenic diseases. They may be
autosomal or sex linked.

steps.label: Haemophilia
steps.why: A woman would need the faulty gene on both her X chromosomes, which is far rarer than a man needing it on his only one.
common_mistakes: Swapping the factors. A is factor VIII, B is factor IX.
Saying it is common in women. It is common in men.
steps.memory_tip: Haemophilia A is factor 8; B is factor 9.
steps.margin_note: Name both types with their clotting factors.
lines: It is a bleeder's disease. Blood does not
clot easily when a wound occurs.
Haemophilia A is due to a deficiency of
clotting factor VIII.
Haemophilia B is due to a deficiency of
clotting factor IX.
It is rare in women, because they need two
recessive genes. It is common in men.

steps.label: Colour blindness
steps.why: Red and green blindness are X-linked but blue blindness is not, which is why the third kind is grouped apart.
common_mistakes: Calling tritanopia sex linked. It is autosomal.
steps.memory_tip: Pro-tan is red, deuter is green, tri is blue.
steps.margin_note: Three named kinds, one line each.
lines: It is a sex linked recessive disorder.
Protanopia is red colour blindness and
deuteranopia is green colour blindness.
Tritanopia is an autosomal disorder called
blue colour blindness.

steps.label: Sickle cell anaemia, PKU
steps.why: Both are recessive, so a carrier is healthy and only a person with two faulty copies shows the disease.
common_mistakes: Giving sickle cell anaemia the wrong chromosome. It is chromosome 11.
Leaving out that it shows only in the homozygous condition.
steps.margin_note: Give the chromosome number for each.
lines: It is an autosomal recessive metabolic
disorder caused by a defective gene on
chromosome 11, expressed in the homozygous
condition.
Symptoms: physical weakness, pain, organ
damage from internal bleeding, paralysis.
It is an autosomal metabolic disorder due
to a gene on chromosome 12. Phenyl ketone
builds up and causes mental retardation.

steps.label: Thalassemia, cystic fibrosis
steps.why: The cystic fibrosis gene controls salt and water movement, so the mucus everywhere in the body becomes thick.
common_mistakes: Placing the cystic fibrosis gene on the wrong chromosome. It is chromosome 7.
steps.memory_tip: Cystic fibrosis: chromosome 7, salty sweat, sticky mucus.
lines: It is an autosomal recessive disorder. The
patient becomes anaemic.
It is an autosomal recessive disorder. The
affected gene is on the long arm of
chromosome 7 and influences salt and water
movement.
Symptoms: increased sodium and chloride in
sweat, thick sticky mucus building up in
the lungs, pancreas and alimentary canal.

steps.label: Chromosomal disorders
steps.why: A whole chromosome added or lost changes hundreds of genes at once, which is why these disorders affect many organs.
common_mistakes: Leaving out non-disjunction as the cause.
steps.memory_tip: Mono is one missing, tri is one extra.
steps.margin_note: Define both words before the examples.
lines: These are caused by the addition or
deletion of a chromosome, or by accidental
exchange of chromosomal bits during meiosis
and non-disjunction.
When a chromosome is deleted from a pair it
is monosomy.
When a chromosome is added to a pair it is
trisomy.

steps.label: Klinefelter, Turner, Down
steps.why: The first two involve the sex chromosomes and the third an autosome, which is why their effects are so different.
common_mistakes: Swapping Klinefelter and Turner. 47,XXY is Klinefelter; 45,X is Turner.
Giving Down syndrome the wrong pair. It is trisomy of pair 21.
steps.memory_tip: Klinefelter 47 XXY, Turner 45 X, Down trisomy 21.
steps.margin_note: Give the karyotype and one or two symptoms for each.
lines: Trisomy of the 23rd pair in males, written
as 47,XXY. Symptoms: hypogonadism, reduced
fertility, slight enlargement of breasts.
Monosomy of the 23rd pair in females,
written as 45,X. Symptoms: flat chest,
short stature, webbed neck, no Barr bodies.
Trisomy of pair 21. Symptoms: delay in
physical and mental development, small
round head, furrowed tongue, open mouth.

steps.label: Edwards, Patau, Cri-du-chat, CML
steps.why: Chronic myeloid leukaemia is not an added or lost chromosome but a swap of pieces between two chromosomes, which is why it causes a cancer rather than a syndrome present from birth.
common_mistakes: Swapping Edwards and Patau. Edwards is 18, Patau is 13.
Describing CML as a trisomy. It is a translocation.
steps.margin_note: Four short entries close the essay.
lines: Trisomy of the 18th pair, more common in
females. Symptoms: cardiac abnormalities
and kidney malfunction.
Trisomy of the 13th pair. Symptoms: heart
and kidney defects, brain and spinal cord
abnormalities, poorly developed eyes.
Partial deletion of the short arm of
chromosome 5. Symptoms: cat like cry,
mental retardation, small head.

lines.text: CML: a piece of chromosome 9 and 22 swap

insider_note: Split the answer in two halves — Mendelian, then chromosomal — and give each disorder its own line with the chromosome number. The numbers are what the examiner ticks.
